PullRequest.Title: Re-diff only the changed response while a chat reply streams
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Refs #328610
Refs #316407

This is a partial fix. It removes the chat list's share of the per-update cost in long chats. Other per-update work that grows with transcript length is still there; see [Follow-ups](#follow-ups).

## Problem

When a reply streams into a long chat, every streamed chunk makes the renderer re-check the entire transcript. With the same reply, a session with 2,000 earlier turns used 4.1× the renderer script time of a 20-turn session (median 3,051 ms vs 748 ms on `main` at `cd2259b`), and the main thread was 91% busy for the whole stream.

**With this PR**, the same reply into the 2,000-turn session takes about half the renderer CPU: median script time drops from 3,051 ms to 1,521 ms, and the main thread is 74% busy instead of 91%. 20-turn sessions are unchanged (748 → 786 ms, within run-to-run noise).

At the stream rate used here (one chunk about every 32 ms), the visible text already kept up on both builds. The median time between visible updates is 32–35 ms either way. So the gain is CPU headroom for typing and other work during a stream, not visibly smoother text.

The 2,000-turn session still costs 1.6–1.9× the 20-turn session (3.7–4.3× on `main`). The rest of that cost comes from code outside the chat list (see [Follow-ups](#follow-ups)).

## Root cause

Every progress event on a response fires the view model's `onDidChange` with `null` ([chatViewModel.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1e81fc75bb564738c29771d9b17c72e708a8211c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatViewModel.ts#L379-L381)). `ChatWidget` batches those events and refreshes the list ([chatWidget.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1e81fc75bb564738c29771d9b17c72e708a8211c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts#L3073-L3089)). `ChatListWidget.refresh()` then rebuilds the whole request/response tree, builds a diff identity string for every item, and calls `setChildren(null, allItems, { diffDepth: 1 })` ([chatListWidget.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1e81fc75bb564738c29771d9b17c72e708a8211c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListWidget.ts#L914-L975)).

In the tree, `spliceSmart` diffs every request. Because `diffDepth` is 1, it also recurses into every unchanged request ([indexTreeModel.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1e81fc75bb564738c29771d9b17c72e708a8211c/src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/indexTreeModel.ts#L194-L208)). Each recursion calls `getParentNodeWithListIndex`, which adds up the row counts of all earlier requests ([indexTreeModel.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1e81fc75bb564738c29771d9b17c72e708a8211c/src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/indexTreeModel.ts#L720-L740)).

So one streamed chunk costs time proportional to the square of the transcript length, plus a string per item, even though only the streaming response changed. In a CPU profile of a 100-chunk reply streamed into the 2,000-turn session on `main` (at `1e81fc7`, when this PR was opened), `ChatListWidget.refresh` took 1,946 ms (46% of the profile), compared with 610 ms with 20 turns. The difference is tree diffing; re-rendering the changed row costs the same at both sizes.

## Fix

- `ChatViewModel` now fires `{ kind: 'changeResponse', response }` instead of `null` when a response changes.
- `ChatWidget` passes the batched events to `ChatListWidget.refresh(changes)`.
- `refresh()` remembers what its last full refresh rendered: the items, each item's diff identity, which requests follow another request, the request being edited, and the visibility and setting counters.
- A batch takes the new path only if all of these hold:
  - every event in it is a response change;
  - the item list is the same elements in the same order;
  - none of that remembered state changed;
  - each changed response sits in the tree under a request, and that request's identity is unchanged. A request's identity changes when its response completes or gains content references.
- On that path, the list calls `setChildren(request, itsResponses, { diffIdentityProvider })` for just those requests, inside the same auto-scroll handling as before. This is the same child-level update the full diff would have made, so the tree's stored identities, focus, selection and auto-scroll behave as before.
- Every other refresh is unchanged and still diffs the whole list: added or removed requests, pending and steering messages, undo/redo and checkpoints, request edits, editing mode, visibility or setting changes, filtered lists, and hidden responses.
- The identity expression moved unchanged into `getDiffIdentity()`. The full refresh now computes each item's identity once per refresh and reuses it.

## Before / after

Both recordings show the same 120-chunk reply streaming into the 2,000-turn session in real time, from the first update the overlay reports to just before the stream finishes. The banner at the top states the run's result from the median of three runs: renderer busy % and renderer script time. The box below it updates live with renderer busy % so far and the time between visible updates. The recordings were made when this PR was opened, on `main` at `1e81fc7`; the numbers in [Measurements](#measurements) are from the current base.

### Before

![Before: on main, a 120-chunk reply streams into a 2,000-turn chat with the renderer about 87% busy (2.8 s of script)](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/34a0f38754696edea759d26fbe7e58487e26dd11/20261015-171820-C8-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

![After: with this PR, the same reply into the same chat with the renderer about 69% busy (1.3 s of script), updating as smoothly as on main](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/34a0f38754696edea759d26fbe7e58487e26dd11/20261015-171820-C8-F1/after.gif?raw=true)

## Measurements

Conditions for every number below:

- **Build:** Code OSS dev build (unminified `out/`), `main` at `cd2259bdf72` vs this PR rebased on it. Windows x64, Agents window, `VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1`.
- **Setup:** chat connected to the built-in mock Agent Host (`--enable-mock-agent`), so there is no model or network traffic. Runs were serialized on the same machine.
- **Sessions:** one with 20 earlier turns and one with 2,000. Each turn is a user message, a completed file-read tool call, and about 400 bytes of markdown.
- **Workload:** one reply of 120 small markdown chunks, sent about every 32 ms (about 4.6 s), with two tool calls in the middle.
- **Prompt timeline off** (`sessions.chatTimeline.display: off`, `chat.stickyScroll.enabled: false`). It has its own per-update cost that is being fixed separately, and that cost would hide the chat list's.
- **Runs:** each build did 1 warm-up run and 3 measured runs. Each run streams into the 20-turn session first, then into the 2,000-turn session.

What each metric measures:

- **Renderer script time:** the change in the renderer's `ScriptDuration` (Chrome DevTools Protocol `Performance.getMetrics`) from pressing Enter until the last chunk is on screen.
- **Main thread busy:** the change in `TaskDuration` over the same interval, divided by its wall-clock time.
- **Time between visible updates:** the streaming response's text is sampled once per animation frame. A frame where the text changed counts as a visible update, and the gap is the time between two such frames.

| | `main`, 20 turns | `main`, 2,000 turns | PR, 20 turns | PR, 2,000 turns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Renderer script time per run (ms) | 827 / 748 / 715 | 3,035 / 3,056 / 3,051 | 968 / 786 / 748 | 1,537 / 1,521 / 1,442 |
| Median script time (per chunk) | 748 ms (6.2 ms) | 3,051 ms (25.4 ms) | 786 ms (6.6 ms) | 1,521 ms (12.7 ms) |
| 2,000-turn ÷ 20-turn, per run | | 3.7× / 4.1× / 4.3× | | 1.6× / 1.9× / 1.9× |
| Main thread busy per run | 65 / 43 / 42% | 88 / 91 / 92% | 73 / 66 / 69% | 74 / 77 / 72% |
| Median time between visible updates per run (ms) | 32 / 32 / 32 | 35 / 33 / 32 | 32 / 32 / 32 | 32 / 32 / 32 |
| Longest time between visible updates per run (ms) | 70 / 87 / 68 | 115 / 134 / 104 | 109 / 74 / 91 | 127 / 111 / 144 |

Memory and listeners were measured when this PR was opened (`main` at `1e81fc7`) and were not re-measured after the rebase. They were taken after three forced garbage collections, once after the warm-up and once after the last run (3 more replies per session). The growth was the same on both builds, so this change adds no retention:

- `main`: heap 255.5 → 261.8 MB (+6.3), event listeners 3,229 → 3,356 (+127), DOM nodes 3,569 → 3,839 (+270).
- PR: heap 163.8 → 170.0 MB (+6.2), event listeners 3,177 → 3,303 (+126), DOM nodes 3,531 → 3,791 (+260).

The growth comes from the six new turns the runs add. Absolute heap differed between the two windows; that difference is not attributed to this change.

## Follow-ups

These per-update costs still grow with transcript length and live outside the chat list, so they are left out of this PR. The costs are rough self times from a CPU profile of a 100-chunk reply into the 2,000-turn session on `main` at `1e81fc7`:

- **Agent session approval tracking, about 160 ms.** The `AgentSessionApprovalModel` autorun subscribes to every response's change signal and walks all requests on any change.
- **Generated-image extraction, about 50 ms.** `getGeneratedImageResources` scans the whole transcript on each update.
- **Tool-confirmation observation.** `ChatListItemRenderer.observeToolConfirmations` re-filters `getItems()` and re-keys every response on each view-model change. Its cost was not isolated; it is part of about 65 ms of observable bookkeeping in that profile.
- **`ChatViewModel.computeItems`, about 65 ms including its callees.** It re-filters the whole transcript after every change because the item cache is invalidated on each event.

## How to test

1. Run Code OSS from this branch and open a long chat, or an Agents session with many turns.
2. Send a prompt that streams a long answer. The answer streams and auto-scrolls as before.
3. While it streams, check that these still update the list correctly: tool calls and progress, completion (the request's checkpoint and hover controls), editing a request, undo, and queuing or steering a message.
4. Optional: record a renderer performance trace while streaming into a long chat. `ChatListWidget.refresh` no longer calls `setChildren` on the root for each chunk; it updates only the streaming response under its request.

<details><summary>Automated streaming scenario (mock Agent Host + Agents window)</summary>

1. Save the mock host below as `mock-agent-host.mjs`.
2. Run it from a built checkout with `BS_PORT=8968 node mock-agent-host.mjs`. Keep stdin open, because the server exits when stdin closes. It serves sessions with 20, 500 and 2,000 synthetic turns, and the prompt `stream:K` streams a reply of K chunks.
3. Launch an Agents window with `VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1` and these settings: `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled: true`, `chat.remoteAgentHosts: [{ "address": "ws://127.0.0.1:8968", "name": "BS Mock" }]`, `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable: true`, `sessions.chatTimeline.display: "off"`, `chat.stickyScroll.enabled: false`.
4. Close the sign-in dialog (current builds offer only its close button; older builds show **Continue Without Signing In**), then open the 20- and 2,000-turn sessions once.
5. Run the scenario over CDP. It fails while the 2,000-turn stream costs 2× or more of the 20-turn stream. On `main` at `cd2259b` it fails at 3.7–4.3×; with this PR it measures 1.6–1.9×.

```js
// mock-agent-host.mjs
// Standalone Agent Host server (compiled from the VS Code worktree's out/) with the ScriptedMockAgent.
// - Seeds mock:/bs-t<N> sessions (BS_SIZES, default 20,500,2000) whose history is N synthetic turns
//   (user message + one completed tool call + small assistant markdown).
// - Prompt `stream:K` streams a reply: one markdown part, then K ChatDelta chunks every BS_DELTA_MS ms (default 20),
//   with a tool call + new markdown part every 50 deltas, then turnComplete.
// Read-only use of the checkout. Usage: node mockhost.mjs  (env BS_PORT, BS_UDD, BS_SIZES, BS_DELTA_MS, BS_PART_BYTES)
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import path from 'node:path';

const VSCODE = process.env.BS_VSCODE || process.cwd();
const out = p => pathToFileURL(path.join(VSCODE, 'out', p)).href;
const partBytes = Number(process.env.BS_PART_BYTES || 400);
const deltaMs = Number(process.env.BS_DELTA_MS || 20);
const sizes = (process.env.BS_SIZES || '20,500,2000').split(',').map(Number);
process.env.VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_MOCK_SEED_SESSIONS = sizes.map(n => `mock:/bs-t${n}`).join(',');

const mock = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mockAgent.js'));
const fx = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/historyRecordFixtures.js'));
const { URI } = await import(out('vs/base/common/uri.js'));

function filler(seed, n, md) {
	const lines = [];
	let size = 0;
	let k = 0;
	while (size < n) {
		const line = md
			? (k % 8 === 0 ? `### Step ${seed}.${k}\n` : `- Item ${seed}.${k}: updated \`module${k % 37}.ts\` to handle edge case ${k * 7 % 101}.\n`)
			: `export function f${seed}_${k}(x: number): number { return x * ${k % 13} + ${seed % 17}; }\n`;
		lines.push(line);
		size += line.length;
		k++;
	}
	return lines.join('');
}

function buildTurns(n, S) {
	const records = [];
	for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		records.push({ type: 'message', role: 'user', session: S, messageId: `u-${i}`, content: `Turn ${i}: please update module${i % 37}.ts and explain the change.` });
		records.push({ type: 'tool_start', session: S, toolCallId: `tc-${i}`, toolName: 'view', displayName: 'Read File', invocationMessage: `Reading module${i % 37}.ts`, toolInput: JSON.stringify({ path: `/src/module${i % 37}.ts` }) });
		records.push({ type: 'tool_complete', session: S, toolCallId: `tc-${i}`, result: { success: true, pastTenseMessage: `Read module${i % 37}.ts`, content: [{ type: 'text', text: filler(i, 200, false) }] } });
		records.push({ type: 'message', role: 'assistant', session: S, messageId: `a-${i}`, content: `Done with turn ${i}.\n\n` + filler(i, partBytes, true) });
	}
	const t = fx.buildTurnsFromHistory(records);
	process.stderr.write(`[bs-mock] built turns=${t.length} json=${(JSON.stringify(t).length / 1048576).toFixed(2)}MB\n`);
	return t;
}
const cache = new Map();
const turnsFor = (n, S) => { if (!cache.has(n)) { cache.set(n, buildTurns(n, S)); } return cache.get(n); };

const P = mock.ScriptedMockAgent.prototype;
const origGet = P.getSessionMessages;
P.getSessionMessages = async function (session) {
	const res = await origGet.call(this, session);
	const str = decodeURIComponent(session.toString());
	if (str.includes('subagent')) { return res; }
	const m = /bs-t(\d+)/.exec(str);
	process.stderr.write(`[bs-mock] getSessionMessages ${str} -> ${m ? m[1] : 'orig'}\n`);
	if (m) { return turnsFor(Number(m[1]), URI.parse(`mock:/bs-t${m[1]}`)); }
	return res;
};
const label = s => { const n = /bs-t(\d+)/.exec(String(s)); return n ? `BS history ${n[1]} turns` : undefined; };
const origFireDisc = P.fireDiscoveredChats;
P.fireDiscoveredChats = function (chats) {
	return origFireDisc.call(this, chats.map(m => ({ ...m, external: false, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })));
};
for (const k of ['listExternalChats', 'listSessions']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { return (await o.apply(this, a)).map(m => ({ ...m, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })); };
}
for (const k of ['getSessionMetadata', 'getChatMetadata']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { const r = await o.apply(this, a); const l = label(String(a[1]?.toString?.() ?? '') + String(a[0])); return r && l ? { ...r, summary: l } : r; };
}
const origDesc = P.getDescriptor;
P.getDescriptor = function () {
	if (!this.__bsRefire) {
		this.__bsRefire = true;
		for (const ms of [1500, 5000]) {
			setTimeout(() => { void this.listExternalChats().then(chats => { process.stderr.write('[bs-mock] refire discovered chats ' + chats.length + '\n'); this.fireDiscoveredChats(chats); }); }, ms);
		}
	}
	return origDesc.call(this);
};

// Streaming: replace 'Unknown prompt: stream:K' with a realistic streamed reply.
const WORDS = ['the', 'parser', 'now', 'handles', '`edge`', 'cases', 'and', 'returns', '**early**', 'when', 'input', 'is', 'empty;', 'see', '`module7.ts`', 'for', 'details.'];
let partSeq = 0;
const origFire = P._fireSequence;
P._fireSequence = function (signals) {
	const first = signals[0];
	const m = first?.action?.part && typeof first.action.part.content === 'string' && /^Unknown prompt: stream:(\d+)/.exec(first.action.part.content);
	if (!m) { return origFire.call(this, signals); }
	const K = Number(m[1]);
	const resource = first.resource;
	const turnId = first.action.turnId;
	const act = action => ({ kind: 'action', resource, action });
	const seq = [];
	let part = `bs-st-${++partSeq}`;
	seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/responsePart', turnId, part: { kind: 'markdown', id: part, content: `## Streamed reply\n\nStarting the change.\n\n` } }));
	let tool = 0;
	for (let i = 1; i <= K; i++) {
		const w = WORDS[i % WORDS.length];
		const content = (i % 12 === 0) ? `${w}\n\n- point ${i}: ` : `${w} `;
		seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/delta', turnId, partId: part, content }));
		if (i % 50 === 0 && i < K) {
			const tc = `bs-tc-${partSeq}-${++tool}`;
			seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/toolCallStart', turnId, toolCallId: tc, toolName: 'view', displayName: 'Read File' }));
			seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/toolCallReady', turnId, toolCallId: tc, invocationMessage: `Reading module${tool}.ts`, toolInput: JSON.stringify({ path: `/src/module${tool}.ts` }), confirmed: 'not-needed' }));
			seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/toolCallComplete', turnId, toolCallId: tc, result: { success: true, pastTenseMessage: `Read module${tool}.ts`, content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'ok' }] } }));
			part = `bs-st-${++partSeq}`;
			seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/responsePart', turnId, part: { kind: 'markdown', id: part, content: `\n\nContinuing after reading module${tool}.ts: ` } }));
		}
	}
	seq.push(act({ type: 'chat/delta', turnId, partId: part, content: `\n\nBS-STREAM-DONE-${K}` }));
	seq.push(signals[signals.length - 1]);
	process.stderr.write(`[bs-mock] stream ${K} deltas (${seq.length} signals) every ${deltaMs} ms turn=${turnId}\n`);
	let i = 0;
	const t0 = Date.now();
	const timer = setInterval(() => {
		const s = seq[i++];
		this._onDidChatProgress.fire(s);
		if (i >= seq.length) { clearInterval(timer); process.stderr.write(`[bs-mock] stream done in ${Date.now() - t0} ms\n`); }
	}, deltaMs);
};

process.argv = [process.argv[0], process.argv[1], '--enable-mock-agent', '--port', process.env.BS_PORT || '0', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--without-connection-token', '--quiet', '--user-data-dir', process.env.BS_UDD || path.join(process.env.TEMP, 'mock-agent-host-udd')];
await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostServerMain.js'));
```

```js
// repro.cjs
// Streaming a reply into a long Agents session costs renderer time proportional to the whole transcript.
//
// Precondition: a Code OSS Agents window
// (VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1) connected via chat.remoteAgentHosts to a mock Agent Host
// (mock-agent-host.mjs below: ScriptedMockAgent, no model traffic) that lists sessions with 20 and 2000 prior turns.
// The prompt `stream:K` streams one reply of K small markdown deltas (plus a tool call every 50 deltas).
// The prompt timeline is turned off (sessions.chatTimeline.display=off, chat.stickyScroll.enabled=false) so that
// its known per-update cost (being fixed separately) is excluded: what remains is the chat list itself.
const K = 120;
const RATIO_LIMIT = 2; // appending the same reply should not cost much more because older turns exist

const OVERLAY = (text) => {
	let el = document.getElementById('bs-overlay');
	if (!el) {
		el = document.createElement('div');
		el.id = 'bs-overlay';
		el.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);top:6px;z-index:100000;background:#000d;color:#fff;font:600 16px monospace;padding:8px 12px;border:2px solid #f80;border-radius:6px;white-space:pre;pointer-events:none';
		document.body.appendChild(el);
	}
	el.textContent = text;
};

async function dismissSignIn(page) {
	const cont = page.getByText('Continue Without Signing In');
	if (await cont.count()) { await cont.first().click().catch(() => { }); await page.waitForTimeout(500); }
}

const maxIdx = page => page.evaluate(() => Math.max(-1, ...[...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row.request, .monaco-list-row.response')].filter(e => e.offsetParent).map(e => Number(e.dataset.index))));

// Session rows under the "Agent mock" group; a session with N prior turns shows ~2N list items.
async function findSession(page, n) {
	const ids = await page.evaluate(() => {
		const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')];
		const header = rows.findIndex(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Agent mock'));
		return header < 0 ? [] : rows.slice(header + 1).filter(r => /^Session,/.test(r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '')).map(r => r.id);
	});
	for (const id of ids) {
		await dismissSignIn(page);
		await page.locator(`[id="${id}"]`).click();
		const ok = await page.waitForFunction(([n, id]) => {
			if (document.getElementById(id)?.getAttribute('aria-selected') !== 'true') { return false; }
			const idx = [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row.request, .monaco-list-row.response')].filter(e => e.offsetParent).map(e => Number(e.dataset.index));
			const max = Math.max(-1, ...idx);
			return max >= 2 * n - 1 && max < 2 * n + 80;
		}, [n, id], { timeout: 8000, polling: 100 }).then(() => true, () => false);
		if (ok) { await page.waitForTimeout(1500); return id; }
	}
	throw new Error(`No mock session with ${n} prior turns found (rows: ${ids.join(', ')})`);
}

const median = a => { const s = [...a].sort((x, y) => x - y); return s.length ? s[Math.floor((s.length - 1) / 2)] : NaN; };

async function streamAndMeasure(ctx, n, label) {
	const { page, cdp } = ctx;
	await findSession(page, n);
	const input = page.locator('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor:visible').last();
	await input.click();
	await page.keyboard.type(`stream:${K}`, { delay: 5 });
	await cdp.send('Performance.enable');
	const metrics = async () => Object.fromEntries((await cdp.send('Performance.getMetrics')).metrics.map(m => [m.name, m.value]));
	// Typing latency: keydown event timestamp -> first DOM mutation of the composer's view lines.
	await page.evaluate(() => {
		window.__bsLat = [];
		window.__bsKeyTs = undefined;
		window.__bsKeyHandler && window.removeEventListener('keydown', window.__bsKeyHandler, true);
		window.__bsKeyHandler = e => { if (e.key === 'x') { window.__bsKeyTs = e.timeStamp; } };
		window.addEventListener('keydown', window.__bsKeyHandler, true);
		window.__bsMo?.disconnect();
		const lines = [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor .view-lines')].filter(e => e.offsetParent).at(-1);
		window.__bsMo = new MutationObserver(() => { if (window.__bsKeyTs !== undefined) { window.__bsLat.push(Math.round(performance.now() - window.__bsKeyTs)); window.__bsKeyTs = undefined; } });
		window.__bsMo.observe(lines, { subtree: true, childList: true, characterData: true });
	});
	const before = await maxIdx(page);
	// Visible updates: sample the streaming response's text once per animation frame; a frame whose text differs
	// from the previous frame is a visible update. Gaps between them show how smoothly the reply streams.
	await page.evaluate(() => {
		window.__bsGaps = [];
		window.__bsLastText = undefined;
		window.__bsLastUpdate = undefined;
		window.__bsSampling = true;
		const sample = () => {
			if (!window.__bsSampling) { return; }
			const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row.response')].filter(e => e.offsetParent);
			const last = rows.sort((a, b) => Number(b.dataset.index) - Number(a.dataset.index))[0];
			const text = last && last.textContent.includes('Streamed reply') ? last.textContent : undefined;
			if (text !== undefined && text !== window.__bsLastText) {
				const now = performance.now();
				if (window.__bsLastUpdate !== undefined && window.__bsLastText !== undefined) { window.__bsGaps.push(now - window.__bsLastUpdate); }
				window.__bsLastUpdate = now;
				window.__bsLastText = text;
			}
			requestAnimationFrame(sample);
		};
		requestAnimationFrame(sample);
	});
	const m0 = await metrics();
	const t0 = Date.now();
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Streaming a response while a long chat transcript is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A response-model change synchronously invalidates ChatViewModel's visible-items cache, Event.accumulate coalesces changes for the current timer turn, ChatWidget calls ChatListWidget.refresh, and the list synchronously computes visible items and updates the ObjectTree before the streamed content is rendered. The PR keeps the existing full-array visibility/equality scan but replaces the root tree diff with a diff under the changed response's request when cached rendered state is valid.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible transcript length N controls the pre-existing getItems/equality scan; response children under the affected request control the changed tree diff, typically one. Accumulated distinct changed requests K are deduplicated, with the common streaming case K=1.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event.accumulate coalesces synchronous response events into one zero-delay batch. Normally one active response/request is targeted; duplicate events for that request are deduplicated by a Set. There is no asynchronous boundary or parallel worker on this UI path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each response event invalidates _visibleItemsCache, so getItems recomputes the visible transcript before the comparison. A prior full refresh warms _renderedState; matching view model, item identities, editing state, visibility generation, and settings enable the targeted child diff. Cold state or any mismatch falls back to a full refresh. No negative cache or external cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed event payload identifies the response, the accumulated event reaches refresh(changes), and the new setChildren(request, children) limits tree diff input to that request's response children. The tests explicitly compare 5-turn and 100-turn transcripts and observe five targeted elements in both.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The remaining array scan still scales with transcript length, and exact DOM/tree-diff savings depend on transcript size and stream cadence, but this scan and cache invalidation predate the PR. The added retained maps/sets are bounded by the current transcript and replace on the next full refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff reduces repeated synchronous tree-diff work from the whole transcript to the affected request for the primary streaming scenario; its new cached state is bounded and lifecycle-reset on view-model or full-refresh changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Structural transcript, editing, visibility, settings, and checkpoint changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same synchronous ChatWidget refresh path runs, but add/remove/null events, item-identity changes, editing changes, visibility-generation changes, setting changes, or request diff-identity changes reject the fast path and execute the existing full root refresh. Checkpoint operations can change many response blocked states in one accumulated batch, but the changed request identity causes an early full-refresh fallback rather than per-request targeted updates.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible chat items N, with one coalesced full tree refresh per event batch. Hover widgets cap visible items at two and do not pass targeted changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are accumulated into one timer-turn callback and one full refresh. The refresh is serialized on the UI thread; no limiter is relevant because no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cached rendered state is deliberately invalidated on setViewModel and replaced after every full refresh. Visibility and setting counters, item equality, editing identity, and cached request diff IDs prevent reusing it across state changes that require a full tree diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every fallback predicate and the request-identity guard is explicit in refreshChangedResponses, and unchanged callers that do not provide response changes continue to call refresh without entering the fast path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Full refresh cost remains proportional to the visible transcript as before. The frequency of bulk checkpoint changes varies, but the changed code does not increase their boundary calls, concurrency, or tree-refresh cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Non-streaming and bulk state changes preserve the previous full-refresh behavior, while the added cache is bounded to the current view model and transcript.

Scenarios.Scenario: Response updates while the chat widget is hidden, followed by showing it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: While hidden, ChatWidget.onDidChangeItems does not call the list refresh, so response updates remain off the rendering critical path. Showing the widget increments visibleChangeCount and schedules an explicit refresh; because no response-change batch is supplied and progressive rendering must restart, that refresh uses the full path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current transcript size at show time; hidden stream event count does not multiply list refreshes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hidden updates may continue arriving and be accumulated, but no list/tree work is performed until the serialized show-time refresh on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The prior rendered state may remain retained while hidden, bounded by the current transcript. The changed visibility generation prevents a stale targeted refresh when the widget is shown, and the next full refresh replaces the cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ChatWidget gates refresh on visibility, increments visibleChangeCount on visibility changes, and the new state comparison rejects fast reuse across that change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of hidden updates and transcript size vary, but the PR does not add eager hidden rendering or any external I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change does not move rendering onto the hidden path and preserves the required one-time full refresh on show.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff hunk. Traced streaming, fallback/bulk-state, and hidden-widget paths through event coalescing, view-model caching, ObjectTree diffing, and lifecycle resets. No actionable performance regression was introduced; the main change bounds synchronous tree diffing during streaming, and no changed or transitive expensive boundary calls were found.
